### Investment Memo: CRWD — 25 November 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD | Conviction: Medium
**Price Target**: $230 (+10% from current $208.97)
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

*Portfolio Strategist report unavailable — construction note prepared by Head of Research. Team disagreement is material: Value values the stock at $95 (Sell), Growth at $250–265 (Buy) — a 2.8x spread. The verdict below sits deliberately between them.*

---

**Investment Thesis**

CrowdStrike is the best-operating franchise in cybersecurity — five consecutive quarters of ARR acceleration to $6.26B (+27%), record net-new ARR (+58%), FCF margin at 30.9% and GAAP operating breakeven reached — but it is priced for perfection at ~35x sales / 118x FCF / ~437x SBC-adjusted FCF, in a macro regime (real yields +57bp, Fed hiking, VIX 36) that is actively repricing exactly this kind of duration asset. The $43.9B all-stock Zscaler acquisition converts a clean organic compounder into a multi-year integration and antitrust story with ~18% dilution. The result: an excellent business whose 12-month risk/reward at $209 is no better than balanced — own less of it, add only on deep drawdowns or deal de-risking.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector is ATTRACTIVE (11–14% CAGR, AI-agent security TAM, consolidation wave favouring platforms) and CRWD's competitive position is STRONG — the only scale vendor re-accelerating. But macro is UNFAVOURABLE: this is a ~20–25yr duration asset facing a real-yield shock with flat breakevens (no nominal offset), an ~80–85% priced December hike, HY OAS +113bp and a +4.9% dollar (1.5–2pt translation headwind). GDP at 3.4% protects revenue; the multiple is what's under attack.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: MEDIUM, rising. ZS deal faces HSR/EU/UK/FDI review with a 20–25% probability of material delay or remedy; all-stock consideration has already eroded from ~$260 to ~$235/ZS share. Live Delta litigation (~$500M claimed) still tests the liability-cap model. EU data-sovereignty package is a structural headwind in the fastest-growing region (EMEA +26%).
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: SELL. Narrow-but-widening moat, fortress balance sheet, but intrinsic value ≈ $95 (range $65–155) even with generous assumptions; SBC at 22.6% of revenue means true owner earnings are ~$479M TTM (9% ROIC ≈ cost of capital). No margin of safety at $209.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY (staged). Five quarters of ARR acceleration, guidance raised 1,060bps, 52% of customers on 6+ modules, Falcon Guardian at $100M ARR in year one, ZS bought at ~13x sales with a ~35x currency. But "buy the growth, rent the valuation" — would not chase above $250.
- **Quantitative Signals**: NEUTRAL. Estimate revisions and target prices rising (mean PT ~$267) while price breaks down: −18.9% in 21 sessions, −25% off the October peak, −8.9% on 4.7x volume post-deal. Value factor 1/10; beta 1.43; 0.85 correlation with PANW. Stabilisation at these levels upgrades the signal; another leg down confirms de-rating.
- **Financial Risk**: LOW credit/liquidity risk (IG at both agencies, $4.5B net cash, nothing due before 2029, FCF positive even in a −20% revenue shock) but HIGH market/valuation risk (52% vol, 0.83% FCF yield). Blended MODERATE. Note: goodwill/intangibles jumped 21% in one quarter to 51% of equity — unexplained M&A, impairment exposure.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. Weak governance (Chairman on Audit Committee during an open SEC revenue-recognition probe, board shrunk 9→8, $247.6M CEO pay +86%), persistent insider selling with zero open-market buys, and the ZS deal layering a second systemic chokepoint (inline network + endpoint agent) into one vendor. DOJ probe closed; SEC leg unresolved after 18+ months.
- **ESG**: AVERAGE / NEUTRAL. Immaterial environmental exposure; dual-class eliminated and independent chair in place; outage litigation largely contained. The only materiality-weighted ESG items are governance: say-on-pay at the June 2027 AGM and ZS deal oversight.
- **Alternative Data**: Bullish on operations, neutral on the equity. Beat sizes are monotonically expanding (5 quarters), record pipeline into Q4, consensus likely still too low for the 9-Mar print. Search/social signals are weak-to-unusable; the −9% reaction on 5x volume is a dilution verdict, not a demand verdict.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: NO EDGE. Explicitly rejects the short: clean Beneish (−3.05), negative accruals, receivables in line, share *gains* per ETR/IDC — the bear case is valuation-only, and shorting 27% growth with net cash is poor risk/reward. Preferred expression: long ZS / short CRWD pair, or stand aside.

---

**Bull Case**
- Only scale security vendor accelerating: ARR +27% (5th straight quarter up), record net-new ARR +58%, 85.7% beat rate with expanding surprises, record Q4 pipeline — consensus still under-forecasting.
- Platform + AI-agent optionality: 6+ module adoption at 52%, Guardian $100M ARR in year one, Nvidia/OpenShell and Anthropic distribution; ZS creates a >$10B ARR platform bought at a 2.7x multiple discount with $1B/$500M synergy targets and claimed immediate FCF-per-share accretion.
- Bulletproof balance sheet: $4.4B+ net cash, 30.9% FCF margin expanding, GAAP breakeven reached, FCF positive even in a −20% revenue shock; all-stock deal structure avoids the debt market entirely.

**Bear Case**
- Zero margin of safety: 35–37x sales, 118x FCF, ~437x SBC-adjusted FCF; every independent intrinsic anchor (DCF $65–155; FY31 consensus capitalised at 25x ≈ 36–40% of today's cap) sits far below the price.
- Hostile duration regime: real yields +57bp with anchored breakevens, Fed hiking into 3.8% CPI, credit +113bp, USD +4.9%; at 1.43 beta, a 20% index drawdown implies ~−29% here. Bear path: multiple compresses to 20–22x → $120–140.
- Deal + governance overhang: ~18% dilution for a −4% GAAP op-margin asset, 20–25% antitrust delay/remedy risk, all-stock reflexivity (a falling CRWD cheapens its own currency), an open SEC rev-rec probe, and zero insider conviction buying into the drawdown.

---

**Key Risks**
1. Multiple compression driven by rates, not earnings — the dominant risk; a 1-sigma year at 52–63% vol is ±half the position.
2. Zscaler: Second Request/EU Phase 2, forced remedies, integration churn on overlapping SKUs, or deal re-cut if CRWD stock keeps falling. Watch the arb spread (~15%) as a live probability gauge.
3. SEC revenue-recognition/ARR probe — unresolved after 18+ months; any restatement is a thesis-changer.
4. SBC persistence: if SBC/revenue doesn't break below 20% post-deal, the FCF narrative degrades.
5. Delta/liability-cap ruling; a second Falcon-class outage (now with inline network exposure post-close).
6. Net-new ARR deceleration in any single quarter — at this multiple, the first 5pt slowdown is worth 30–40% of market cap.

---

**Portfolio Construction Note** (Head of Research, in lieu of Portfolio Strategist)

- **Treat CRWD as a cybersecurity factor position, not an idiosyncratic one**: 0.85 correlation with PANW and 0.63 with ZS means consolidated cyber exposure should be sized as a single bucket. Cap CRWD at **1.5–2.5% of NAV** given 1.43 beta and 52%+ vol.
- **Discipline levels**: trim above ~$250 (Growth's own ceiling); add only below ~$150 or on two confirmations — (a) deal cleared with minor remedies and (b) ARR growth holding >20%. Current price is in no-man's land between those triggers.
- **Event calendar as risk gates**: December FOMC (8–9 Dec, hike ~85% priced), HSR filing deadline (5 Jan 2027), Q4 FY27 print + initial FY28 guide (9 Mar 2027). Consider collars or reduced gross into each.
- **For accounts able to run pairs**: long ZS / short CRWD captures the ~15% arb spread while hedging sector beta — the Short analyst's preferred structure and a cleaner expression than outright shorting.
- **Do not double-count the drawdown**: −27% from October has already absorbed part of the compression; that, plus positive revisions, is why this is a HOLD and not a SELL. It becomes a SELL on a confirmed second leg down through ~$180 on volume, or an SEC/enforcement escalation.

*Data gaps flagged by the team: NRR %, ZS pro-forma SBC detail, say-on-pay support, country-level revenue, and CDS/revolver terms were unavailable; the FY27 international split is approximate. Peer multiples rest on a 4-name cyber set.*

---

## 1. Sector Overview

Cybersecurity is a ~$244bn end-user spend market in CY2026 growing ~11–12% in constant currency (Gartner 3Q26), with a second forecast house (IDC) at $362bn for 2027 — a ~$86bn spread that itself signals how poorly the market is bounded. Growth is structurally underwritten (89% of firms report AI-enabled attacks per BCG's 2026 CISO survey) but the *incremental* dollar is rotating fast toward AI-agent security, identity and cloud/network — the segments where CrowdStrike has been thinnest. The industry is mid-cycle in a **platform-consolidation wave**: 2026 is tracking the highest cyber M&A deal count on record, headlined by Google/Wiz ($32bn), Palo Alto/CyberArk, and now **CrowdStrike/Zscaler ($43.9bn all-stock, 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share, 34% premium, announced 23-Nov-2026)**. Pure-play growth has decelerated from the 40–60% pandemic era to a 12–30% band, so multiple expansion now depends on consolidation-driven cross-sell and the AI-agent TAM rather than on category growth alone. Concentration remains modest (PANW ~11.5% share in 1Q26, per Jay McBain/Channel data) — i.e., a **fragmented, consolidating market with low HHI and rising scale advantages**, not a mature oligopoly.

---

## 2. Key Tailwinds

- **AI-agent security is opening a genuine new budget line, not a re-labelling.** 69% of CISOs name AI as their top net-new investment priority; Gartner puts total AI spending at $2.52tn in 2026 (+44%) and IT spending at $7.35tn in 2027 (+15%). Nvidia named CrowdStrike a partner on its OpenShell agent-containment framework (BlueField-4/Sentry) — a distribution and standard-setting tailwind for Falcon.
- **Consolidation is a share-gain engine for scale platforms.** Buyers are collapsing 30–60 point tools into 2–3 platforms; PANW grew share from 9.7% to 11.5% in a year largely via CyberArk. Post-ZS, CRWD adds network/zero-trust and management claims a **~$185bn TAM expansion**.
- **Regulatory and disclosure mandates are converting cyber from discretionary to non-discretionary.** New US requirements for AI companies to report security incidents, plus breach-disclosure regimes, structurally raise baseline spend; 72% of surveyed enterprises name cyber as a 2027 new-investment priority.

## 3. Key Headwinds

- **Budget growth is decelerating and being reallocated, not expanded.** Cyber budgets grew only ~5% in 2026 (TechTarget/ETR), and the $100k–$499k mid-market band is compressing — growth is increasingly a share fight, favouring platforms over point solutions.
- **Deal risk and dilution.** CRWD fell ~9% on the ZS announcement; $43.9bn of stock issuance against a ~$6bn-revenue base is a ~7x revenue multiple paid in the most expensive currency in the sector, and closing is not until 2H FY2028. Integration/attrition risk is real (see PANW/CyberArk's post-deal margin compression).
- **Margin structure is under pressure sector-wide.** GAAP operating margins for the growth cohort remain negative-to-low, and the two most profitable players (FTNT 30.7%, CHKP 30.5%) are the *slowest* growers (14%, 6%) — the sector is being asked to pay for growth with gross margin (PANW GM fell 74.4%→70.4% in two years).

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **STRONG**

- **Growth re-acceleration is the standout datapoint in the peer set.** CRWD's YoY growth troughed at +21.7% in FY26 and has since re-accelerated to +28.3% in Q3 FY27 ($1.583bn vs $1.234bn), with ARR +27% to $6.26bn and $419m of net-new ARR in the quarter. No scale peer is inflecting upward at that size.
- **Margin trajectory is best-in-class on the improvement axis.** GAAP operating margin has gone from -8.5% (FY23) → -6.1% (FY26) → roughly breakeven (-0.05%) in Q3 FY27, while gross margin held at ~75% — i.e., the operating leverage is arriving *without* the gross-margin erosion PANW accepted.
- **But: the valuation is the position's main vulnerability.** At ~35x FY27E sales (34x ARR) versus a ~21x peer median and ~11–12x for ZS/FTNT, CRWD embeds near-flawless ZS integration. The stock is **-27% from its 6-Oct-2026 high of $286.99** yet still **+78% YTD** and +141% since Jan-2025 — a crowded, high-beta (1.15) name where the ZS dilution math (1.135x share count exchange) is the single largest swing factor.
- **Competitive moat:** high switching costs and multi-module land-and-expand (strong), network effects via threat telemetry (moderate-strong), capital intensity low (favourable). Weakness: endpoint heritage leaves network/zero-trust and identity — precisely what ZS buys — plus a well-funded Microsoft bundling threat.

**Porter's Five Forces (sector):** Rivalry HIGH (consolidating, price/bundle pressure); Buyer power MODERATE-HIGH (platform deals, CIO consolidation); Supplier power LOW; New entrants MODERATE (AI-native startups, but enterprise trust is a barrier); Substitutes MODERATE (hyperscaler-native security).

---

## 6. Sector Rating: **ATTRACTIVE** (with a valuation caveat)

**Rationale:** 11–14% underlying market CAGR, a genuine new AI-agent security TAM, non-discretionary regulatory demand, and a consolidation wave that rewards exactly the platform scale CRWD now has. Cycle position: **late-stage high growth / early consolidation** — decelerating category growth but rising winner-take-most dynamics, which is favourable for the top three and hostile to the tail. The offset is that public multiples already discount the consolidation thesis (CRWD 35x, NET 37x sales), so sector returns from here are likely to be **share-gain-driven rather than multiple-driven**. Rating would move to Neutral on: (a) cyber budget growth sustaining below 5%, or (b) evidence that AI security spend is being captured by hyperscalers/model vendors rather than by security platforms.

## CRWD — Geopolitical & Legal Risk Assessment
*As of 23 Nov 2026 | Sources: CRWD 10-Q/10-K, IR releases, SEC Form 425, Reuters, CNBC, court records*

**Headline event:** CRWD signed a definitive agreement (22 Nov 2026) to acquire **Zscaler (ZS)** for **~$43.9B all-stock** (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share, ~34% premium) — the largest cybersecurity M&A on record. Expected close: **H2 FY2028 (Aug 2027–Jan 2028)**, subject to Zscaler shareholder vote, HSR/EU/UK/other clearances and foreign-investment approvals; antitrust filings due by **5 Jan 2027**; outside date late 2027. CRWD fell **~11%** on announcement. This transaction now dominates the legal/regulatory risk profile.

---

### 1. Geographic Risk Map

FY2026 (ended 31 Jan 2026), total revenue **$4.81B** (Bullfincher/FMP, from 10-K). FY2026 10-Q confirms **no country other than the US represents ≥10% of revenue**, so country-level granularity below region is inferred, not disclosed.

| Region | FY26 Rev | % of Total | YoY | Primary Countries (est.) | Risk Level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **United States** | $3.217B | **66.9%** | +19.9% | US | **Medium** |
| **EMEA** | $782.7M | **16.3%** | +26.3% | UK, Germany, France, Nordics, UAE/KSA | **Medium-High** |
| **Asia Pacific** | $495.7M | **10.3%** | +23.2% | Japan, Australia, India, Singapore | **Medium** |
| **Other** (Canada, LatAm, rest) | $317.0M | **6.6%** | +27.4% | Canada, Brazil, Mexico | **Medium** |

**Key structural read:** international is only 33% of revenue but is growing **~1.3–1.4x faster** than the US (EMEA +26%, Other +27%, APAC +23% vs US +20%). Geographic mix is shifting into higher-regulatory-intensity jurisdictions — i.e., risk is rising even without a change in operations. CrowdStrike has no material Russia or mainland China revenue (exited Russia/Belarus post-2022); sovereign/state-directed cyber exposure is a *threat* vector, not a revenue vector.

Q3 FY2027 (qtr ended 31 Oct 2026): revenue **$1.583B, +28%**; subscription $1.503B, +29%; **ARR $6.26B, +27%**; record net new ARR $419M; net income $24.9M.

---

### 2. Top 3 Geopolitical Risks

**① Zscaler antitrust / FDI clearance failure or forced remedy — Probability 20–25% | Impact: High**
The deal merges the #1 endpoint platform with the #1 independent SSE/SASE vendor, pushing CRWD into network security — cybersecurity's largest TAM segment. Overlap in cloud workload protection, Zero Trust and security analytics invites scrutiny from **DOJ/FTC (HSR)**, **EU Commission (potential Phase 2)**, **UK CMA**, and multiple FDI regimes given both firms' government/defense customer bases. Combined ARR >$10B and ~8,000 incremental Zscaler customers means the counterfactual "share of a concentrated market" argument is easy for regulators to make. Base case is clearance with conditions; a Phase 2 EU referral or US Second Request would push close toward/through the late-2027 outside date and re-open financing/valuation risk on an all-stock deal. *Note: all-stock structure means the effective price floats with CRWD — already down 11%, cutting deal value from ~$260 to ~$235/share within a day.*

**② EU–US data sovereignty divergence — Probability 70% (package advances), scope uncertain | Impact: Medium**
The European Commission's **Tech Sovereignty Package** (expected 27 May 2026) would restrict EU member-state governments from using US cloud providers for sensitive public-sector data (healthcare, finance, judicial), driven explicitly by the **US CLOUD Act**. Requires approval of all 27 member states; would not ban US providers outright but sets a procurement floor of "sovereignty you can prove." CrowdStrike is a US-headquartered processor of deeply sensitive security telemetry — even as a security vendor rather than a hyperscaler, it sits in the blast radius. Mitigants: **STACKIT sovereign cloud partnership** (Schwarz Digits, Germany) and CRWD's Global Data Sovereignty programme; FedRAMP High since 2018. Direct EMEA public-sector exposure is a minority of the 16% EMEA slice, capping total impact, but reputational spillover into EU private-sector procurement is the real risk.

**③ US federal procurement & nation-state threat concentration — Probability: Medium | Impact: Medium**
Public sector (federal/SLTT) is a disproportionate revenue contributor relative to the 67% US share, tied to FedRAMP High, CISA BOD-26-04 and CMMC mandates. Exposure to federal budget cycles, procurement-efficiency reviews, and shutdowns is structural. Concurrently, CRWD is a tier-one target for Russian/Chinese state APTs precisely because of that government footprint — a successful intrusion would carry existential reputational weight (the July 2024 outage showed the demand-side fragility of trust).

---

### 3. Legal & Regulatory Highlights

**Active litigation (July 19, 2024 outage)**
- **Delta Air Lines v. CrowdStrike** — Fulton County Superior Court (GA), ~**$500M** claimed. May 2025 order granted CRWD's motion to dismiss **in part** (fraud claims dismissed; negligence/breach of contract counts survived). **Still unresolved two years on** — this is the single largest quantified legal contingency and directly tests the enforceability of CRWD's contractual liability caps.
- **Passenger class action** (federal) — **dismissed**, claims preempted by the Montreal Convention/airline tariff.
- **Securities class action** (W.D. Tex., filed 30 Jul 2024) — **dismissed 12 Jan 2026** (Judge Robert Pitman); lead plaintiff filed notice of **appeal 26 Jan 2026** — appeal pending.
- A **cert petition** remains pending before the Supreme Court (CRWD's response deadline extended to 18 Dec 2026); no cert decision yet.

**Regulatory stack (compliance cost, not prohibition)**
- **EU:** GDPR/Schrems II, NIS2, DORA (financial-services clients), EU AI Act (material given SafeMind/agentic AI push and Zscaler "Zero Trust for AI Safety"), EU Data Act.
- **US:** FedRAMP High; CISA BOD-26-04; CMMC; SEC cyber-disclosure rules; state privacy laws.
- **APAC:** Australia SOCI Act/APRA CPS 234, Japan FISC, India DPDP Act.
- **Deal-related:** HSR, EU Merger Regulation, UK CMA/NSIA, plus FDI filings in Australia, Japan, India, Germany, France and likely SAMR.

---

### 4. Compliance Red Flags

1. **Liability-cap enforceability (elevated).** The Georgian court letting negligence and contract claims proceed despite CRWD's contractual limitation of liability is the most under-appreciated risk in the file. Loss of cap enforceability converts every future outage into uncapped exposure and re-prices enterprise contracts industry-wide.
2. **Extensive indirect/channel distribution.** Global reseller, distributor, SI and marketplace model creates third-party diversion and sanctions-screening exposure across Middle East, Türkiye and APAC — a standard **FCPA/AML/sanctions** vector. No active enforcement disclosed, but the control surface is wide.
3. **Data-transfer conflict of laws.** CLOUD Act vs GDPR is irreconcilable by contract; the EU package makes that conflict a procurement disqualifier rather than a fine. DPA/P II-style transfer mechanisms will not cure it.
4. **Encryption/export controls.** US BIS EAR classification of Falcon cryptography — low-probability but non-zero tail risk if export rules tighten.
5. **AI-agent liability.** Selling autonomous remediation/agentic SOC capability raises unresolved questions on who bears liability for an AI-initiated action — no regime yet, but EU AI Act transparency duties attach.

---

### 5. Overall Geopolitical/Legal Risk Rating: **MEDIUM**

**Rationale:** Operating footprint is overwhelmingly in high-rule-of-law jurisdictions (US 67%, with Canada/UK/EU/Australia/Japan the bulk of the rest); no Russia, Iran or mainland China revenue; no active DOJ/SEC/OFC sanctions or FCPA enforcement action disclosed. Set against that: (a) a **transformational $44B merger with a genuine multi-jurisdiction antitrust and FDI path** and a ~20–25% chance of material delay or remedy; (b) live, unresolved **$500M Delta litigation** that threatens the liability-cap model underpinning the entire software industry's risk architecture; (c) a **structural EU–US sovereignty conflict** that is moving from rhetoric to binding procurement law in exactly the region growing fastest (+26%). Risk is **rising, not falling**, as international mix grows.

**What would move this to HIGH:** a DOJ Second Request or EU Phase 2 referral on Zscaler; an adverse Delta verdict on liability-cap enforceability; or the Tech Sovereignty Package emerging with private-sector scope.

**What would move it to LOW:** Delta settled within reserves with caps upheld; Zscaler cleared early (Q1–Q2 CY2027) with only minor divestitures; EU package narrowed to hyperscalers only.

---
*Gaps: CrowdStrike has not yet filed a 10-Q covering the Zscaler transaction, so merger-related risk factors and break-fee terms are not yet in filed form (Form 425/8-K only). Country-level revenue below the regional level is not disclosed. Reuters and one deal-timeline source were paywalled/blocked and were corroborated via SEC Form 425, IR releases and secondary reporting.*

# Macroeconomic Assessment: CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD)

## 1. Macro Environment Summary

**Stance: Transitional, tilting risk-off — a "reflationary overtightening" regime.**

The US economy is *not* slowing into recession. It is re-accelerating into a supply-constrained, inflation-prone expansion, and the Fed has been forced into an abrupt policy reversal. Real GDP grew **3.4% SAAR in Q3 2026** (Q2: 2.2%, Q1: 2.5%), unemployment has fallen to **4.1%** (from 4.5% in Nov-25), and nominal PCE is running **+6.3% YoY** (Sep-26 vs Sep-25). With a ~3.8% CPI deflator on top of 3.4% real growth, **nominal GDP is growing ~7%** — a genuine tailwind for enterprise IT budget pools.

But the price of that growth is being paid in the bond market. The Fed cut from 4.33% (Jul-25) to a 3.63% trough by May-26, then **reversed**: effective fed funds have risen to **3.88% (Oct-26)** with the target range at 3.75–4.00% (held at the 28 Oct FOMC). Markets price an **~80–85% probability of a hike at the 8–9 December meeting**, with another likely by March 2027; the FOMC median dots cluster at 4.00–4.25% for both end-2026 and end-2027. Fed officials (Cook, Waller, Barr) have publicly advocated further hikes.

The critical diagnostic: the 10Y yield has risen from **4.38% (29 Jun) to 5.13%**, peaking at **5.31% on 5 Oct**, while the 10Y breakeven has been *flat-to-lower* (2.24% → 2.13%). The entire move is **real yields** — the 10Y TIPS yield went from **2.20% to 2.77%** (+57bp), and briefly 2.95%. This is the worst possible shape of rate rise for long-duration equities: pure discount-rate compression with **no offsetting inflation-expectation or nominal-growth uplift**.

Risk appetite has cracked. **HY OAS widened from 2.63% (28 Aug) to 3.76% (20 Nov)** — still tight in absolute terms, but +113bp in twelve weeks is a violent repricing. **VIX has jumped from 14.8 (8 Oct) to 35.9 (20 Nov)**. The curve is positively sloped (+39bp 2s10s, bear-steepening) — no recession signal. The risk is a **valuation event, not an earnings recession**.
